item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00314","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C23","C12","C01"],"selected_candidate_label":"C23","confidence":0.91,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C23 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child's discussion of the White House Conference on Education. Both texts move through the Conference's citizen-based character, the classroom shortage and need for Federal assistance, teacher shortages and salaries, local control of education, and the Conference's role in stimulating continuing public action. C12 is also materially related, especially in its Federal–State philosophy and description of the conference machinery, but C23 more closely matches the child's retrospective account and sequence of issues. C01 supports only the narrower passage concerning the Committee on Education Beyond the High School.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Under our system, education is basically a community function. It requires the active support of citizens in their own homes. With this in mind, I initiated the White House Conference on Education.","parent_excerpt":"The Report is important for what it says, and for what it symbolizes--a free and vigorous people working to improve public education. It reflects widespread understanding that public education means public responsibility...but for everybody.","explanation":"Both frame education as a broad citizen responsibility and use that principle to explain the White House Conference."},{"child_excerpt":"The classroom shortage...has been improving now for the past two years... Teachers salaries have been increased in many communities","parent_excerpt":"The Report confirms the critical nature of the classroom shortage in public schools, and recognizes the need for Federal assistance... It recognizes the crucial importance of good teaching, and the need for higher salaries and greater community prestige to attract more teachers.","explanation":"The child reprises the same paired substantive concerns—classroom capacity and teacher recruitment or compensation—treated together in C23."},{"child_excerpt":"Citizen interest and responsibility in educational problems was stirred by this Conference. It gave impetus and direction to a long-felt need for action.","parent_excerpt":"Throughout the State and local conferences, and the White House Conference, your Committee gave effective leadership to a broad awakening of public interest in our schools...only one step in a continuing effort","explanation":"The distinctive retrospective claim that the Conference awakened public interest and initiated continuing action closely parallels C23."},{"child_excerpt":"the role of the Federal Government is to aid, encourage, and facilitate-but never to control--education","parent_excerpt":"control of education should be as close as possible to parents and citizens in the local communities","explanation":"These passages express the same governing principle of limited Federal assistance combined with local control."}]}
